revision.message:
Fix X Article uploads, payload artifacts and blog covers

The full article failed with HTTP 503 because X currently rejects header-three,
although its published schema permits it. Clamp third-level and deeper Markdown
headings to header-two while preserving their text. A controlled full-post upload
succeeded with only that block type changed; the converter now reproduces the
accepted payload. Update the existing conversion checks and mapping contract.

Use 5:2 image files for both existing blog headers, matching X Article cover
display. Add optional aspect-ratio padding to the hermetic Mermaid WebP renderer,
preserve each diagram's complete content and theme, and arrange the upload
pipeline for the wider canvas. Validate intrinsic and displayed dimensions,
content placement, backgrounds, and unchanged default raster behavior.
Encourage optional WebP headers in images with a 5:2 canvas in the blog skill,
and cover the guidance in its existing offline evaluation configuration.

Add the official xurl v1.3.4 CLI through a checksum-pinned Linux x86-64 toolchain
and repository wrapper for independent API diagnostics.

Nest X request fields under payload and retain local media locators alongside
it. Report diagnostics only to stderr, fail command conversion on warnings by
default, and allow an explicit warnings-as-errors override. Reject legacy flat
artifacts before upload and attach resolved banner IDs inside the payload.
Validate the CLI contract with executable E2E cases and update its specification
and upload guidance.

Expand the blog explanation with example X payload and offline artifact JSON,
clarify Hugo render-hook limitations and media resolution, and align its heading
showcase with the upload fix. Preserve the reviewed author wording.

OpenSpec-Change: projects/x_article_uploader/openspec/changes/wrap-article-payload

commits.message:
Merge pull request #92 from alwaldend/t3code/polish-mermaid-diagram-styling

Render hermetic Mermaid diagrams and publish the migration post

Merge pull request #95 from alwaldend/t3code/consolidate-project-landing-pages

Move project landings into the main site

Manage forge resources with hermetic Terraform rules

Centralize organization, repository, and named access configuration in
infra/repos. Adopt existing GitHub resources, protect master defaults while
retaining Pages publication on pages, and preserve existing repository
identities. Manage GitLab one-time imports, the F-Droid metadata fork, and
default-branch protections through Vault-backed authentication. Forgejo
consumes the same catalog. Ongoing repository synchronization is deferred.

Retire the eleven Bazel rule landing sites through their owning Terraform
workflows, removing their DNS records, Pages repositories, and landing
configuration. Move all twelve existing standalone rule modules into tools/
and retain their public interfaces and documentation on the main site.

Add tools/rules_terraform with verified provider downloads, packed mirrors
in runfiles, and reusable Terraform execution rules. Enforce one version per
provider source at an extensible resolution boundary. Migrate every Terraform
consumer to thirteen shared provider pins in third_party/terraform. Execution
and command maps belong to rules_terraform; consumers explicitly select generic
AL wrappers for authentication and Vault injection. Remove tools/terraform
and all 43 checked-in Terraform provider locks.
Validate installed providers against the declared archives before execution.

Validation covers all fourteen workspace builds, all thirteen standalone
test suites, Terraform consumers, offline real-provider regressions, rendered
documentation, formatting, and semantic lint. The full root test run has
295 passing tests and one skip; its only failure is the historical secret
scan, reduced to four pre-existing synthetic fixture matches. Earlier live
imports and the exact landing retirement scope have verified postconditions;
the Terraform rules migration uses only offline implementation checks.

Deploy project DNS through Terraform modules

Move DNS ownership into each project’s Terraform state using shared modules.
Load dnsconfig.json files at runtime, reject conflicting domain ownership,
and render their records as a table. Add missing project AppRoles and scoped
DNS policies, and document grouping related Terraform resources in modules.

Deploy all 45 owners sequentially: adopt 155 existing records and create 13
missing OpenHands records. Preserve every pre-existing provider record and
verify no-op follow-up plans and DNS answers. Add DNS-scoped plan/show/apply
wrappers with a saved-plan guard for roots that also manage services.
Allow bounded aggregate path inventories large enough to deliver this migration
while retaining truncation refusal in the delivery tool.

Validate runtime ownership, provider imports and preservation with isolated
fixtures, Terraform formatting, wrapper builds, repository quality checks,
semantic lint, and project documentation/specification builds.

AGP, Kotlin, Compose, and protobuf plugin versions once, and derive their

the status bar area follows the system theme, not a default white surface.

Restore light and dark site canvases and set the shared accent

The shared Docsy canvas set the same Bootstrap dark palette and the same
black page background on `:root`, `[data-bs-theme="light"]`, and
`[data-bs-theme="dark"]`, so the light/dark toggle changed nothing. The site
also rendered Bootstrap's stock blue instead of its intended accent.

Split the shared palette so light mode uses a pure white canvas with the
light-mode palette and dark mode uses a pure black canvas with the dark-mode
palette, and keep the pre-stylesheet paint and footer on the active mode.
Assign `$primary` to `#7c3aed` before Bootstrap compiles, so links, buttons,
badges, focus rings, and the dark-mode link tint all derive from one value
rather than from a site-local copy.

Both files stay in the reusable shell; the apex site consumes them through
the existing declared exports and no longer carries the footer's own blue.

Propose native Nexus deployment on XCP-ng

Add an owner-local OpenSpec proposal, design, capability deltas, and
implementation checklist for native Nexus 3 and PostgreSQL on one VM.
Define PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub proxies with Vault-backed configuration
and separate provisioning, Ansible, service Terraform, and Traefik ownership.

This change contains planning artifacts only. Implementation and live
deployment remain outside this handoff.
Register the planning workspace for strict repository validation and document
component ownership. Link a collection-owned PostgreSQL proposal that defines
the reusable role's initialization, authentication, ownership, extension, and
compatibility contracts with their own acceptance tasks.

Publish the X Article story and harden its upload workflow

Publish the reviewed development story and render blog front matter images
before article text and in print output. Remove redundant opening Markdown
images from the two illustrated posts. Keep the first selected image as the
X Article banner and preserve every image explicitly written in Markdown.
Document the shared image metadata and encourage its use for every post.

Retain rate-limit headers on failed X requests and report their reset times
and conservative retry boundaries. Keep retries manual and distinguish
historical quota observations from the latest response. Reject HTTP redirects
without following them so draft and media POSTs cannot be replayed by a
redirect response, and prevent automatic replay of consumed POST bodies.

Recover expired Vault certificates through a host-limited Ansible tag that
stops before reload on certificate errors. Preserve the Vault node identity,
use its canonical connection hostname, and include that name in the certificate.
Document temporary Vault TLS bypass, repository SSH CA trust, and verification
after renewal. The authorized renewal succeeded with normal TLS restored.

Validate static images before network requests and wait for media processing
with signed, bounded status checks. Scope cached media to the endpoint and
OAuth credential context, account for upload time and expiry, and refuse
identifiers that expire while other images upload. Emit mutable Markdown
entities and replace byte counting with an explicitly approximate weighted
budget, preserving the original Markdown source.

Validation: uploader conversion and HTTP E2E tests, site browser and skill checks,
repository quality and semantic lint; packaged Ansible syntax and task selection;
strict OpenSpec validation and live certificate/hostname verification.
